title: Establishment of an EPS security context during inter-system change from N1 mode to S1 mode in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode

entities.name: Inter-system change from N1 mode to S1 mode
entities.description: Procedure for changing from 5G NAS (N1 mode) to EPS NAS (S1 mode) while in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode in single-registration mode with N26 interface support.

entities.name: Mapped EPS security context
entities.description: Security context derived from 5G NAS security context for use in EPS during inter-system change.

entities.name: K'ASME key
entities.description: Derived key for EPS security context created from KAMF and downlink NAS COUNT.

entities.name: N1 mode to S1 mode NAS transparent container IE
entities.description: Information element containing NAS sequence number for inter-system change security context derivation.

entities.name: NAS COUNT
entities.description: Counter value used in NAS security context for key derivation and sequence management.

entities.name: NAS algorithms identifiers
entities.description: Encryption and integrity protection algorithms selected for use in target MME after inter-system change.

entities.name: eKSI
entities.description: EPS Key Set Identifier derived from ngKSI with type field indicating mapped security context.

entities.name: Invalid NAS COUNT condition
entities.description: Condition where received NAS transparent container IE does not have a valid NAS COUNT.

entities.name: Inter-system change failure condition
entities.description: Condition where inter-system change from N1 mode to S1 mode is not completed successfully.

entities.name: 5GMM-CONNECTED mode
entities.description: 5G Mobility Management connected state from which inter-system change is performed.

relations.description: Inter-system change procedure establishes a mapped EPS security context.
Inter-system change requires the UE to be in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode.
Mapped EPS security context contains the derived K'ASME key.
N1 mode to S1 mode NAS transparent container IE contains NAS sequence number (COUNT).
Invalid NAS COUNT condition guards the processing of the NAS transparent container IE.
Inter-system change failure condition establishes deletion of the mapped EPS security context.
Mapped EPS security context contains NAS algorithms identifiers for encryption and integrity protection.
Mapped EPS security context contains the eKSI identifier derived from ngKSI.
